# Independent audit: favorable active menus under common continuous symmetry

Audited `candidate 4978e2e0751c0926` in full. The positive theorem passes.

The affine center shear preserves the mixed lattice, fiber volumes, halfspaces, and the normal-dependent convex physical-field class. A finite common linear symmetry group preserves volume and pooled within-fiber covariance, so the actual smooth cap problem is invariant. The zero common fixed space forces each fiber centroid and each unique deepest own mark to be zero after the shear. Averaging the dual representation gives zero as well, justifying the zero H gradient and the continuous-normal balance.

Orbiting ONE actual cap preserves its base tilt, cap mass, coarea S, and first strip moment A. Equal S is what makes the same orbit weights both quantile and response weights. Caratheodory reduction of the averaged continuous normal therefore preserves the needed actual balanced menu; it does not need any flatness or flexibility in the base tilt.

An exposed vertex q maximizing the fixed base tilt satisfies a.(q-p)>=0. Thus every cap of that SAME orbit contains the centroid-through halfspace in the q-fiber. The explicit finite convex field isolates exactly this complete-base fiber and equals its positive centroid cone height there. Divergence/radial integration gives the exact d|K_q| normalization and ordinary sharp Grünbaum credit for each orbit cap. No integer point is obtained by rounding a continuous centroid: the target is an actual exposed integer base and its continuous centroid lies inside its own fiber.

Summing one normalized field per distinct exposed target gives simultaneous Gamma_d/r credit to every chosen source profile. The positive H response terms and uniform O(epsilon+h) correction then imply the stated actual-descent criterion. The source-weight separator is allowed to depend on this favorable complete menu selection. The theorem does not assume a separator valid for all menus.

The extension to the pure-width model uses only its independently established unique-source and first-response facts and otherwise removes terms from the same argument. Common central symmetry and homothetic simplex families with an AFFINE center graph are valid examples. A nonaffine center graph does not give a global block affine symmetry, and the note correctly excludes it.

No repair is needed. In particular, an isolated active base tilt inside this common-symmetry class is not an obstruction to favorable-menu payment.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
